requirements.quote: Make sure the “deploy” directory exists (create it if necessary) before writing the two files.
YAML structure and ordering must be *exactly*:

check.cmd:
test -s /home/user/deploy/release_summary.yaml && [ "$(sed -E 's/^(    latest_version: )v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/\1V/; s/^(    release_date: )"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}"$/\1D/' /home/user/deploy/release_summary.yaml)" = "$(printf 'services:
  - name: alpha
    latest_version: V
    release_date: D
  - name: beta
    latest_version: V
    release_date: D
  - name: gamma
    latest_version: V
    release_date: D')" ]

requirements.quote: The list items **must appear in the fixed alpha → beta → gamma order** shown above.

check.cmd: [ "$(grep -o 'name: [a-z]*' /home/user/deploy/release_summary.yaml | tr '\n' ' ')" = 'name: alpha name: beta name: gamma ' ]

requirements.quote: The date strings are wrapped in double quotes so that automated parsers keep them as strings.
A plain-text log file containing exactly three lines, one per service, in this strict colon-separated format:
2.  Parse “/home/user/deploy/extraction.log” and validate that every service line contains the exact same version and date values that appear in the YAML file.
*   A final new-line (line-feed) must be present at the end of the file.
*   Both output files must end up world-readable (at least 0644) so that the automated grader can inspect them.
